source_interpretation.title: The solvent comparison is a negative-control observation
source_interpretation.text: Benzene and tetrahydrofuran are reported unable to dissolve selenium powder: no homogeneous solution forms and no PbSe is obtained under gamma irradiation. These are separate negative solvent observations, without individually specified doses or complete procedures.
source_interpretation.source_locator: Supplied main PDF p. 2, solvent-comparison paragraph

source_interpretation.title: Coordination and solvated-electron explanations remain proposed
source_interpretation.text: The authors say the formation mechanism is unknown. They propose that ethylenediamine coordinates and stabilizes Pb(II), helps dissolve/complex selenium and increases its dispersion/reactivity. Solvated electrons formed under irradiation are proposed to activate reduction. No coordination structure, intermediate or kinetic measurement establishes this pathway.
source_interpretation.source_locator: Supplied main PDF p. 1, final paragraph; p. 2, solvent and proposed mechanism

source_interpretation.title: Keep source activity, absorbed dose and elapsed times distinct
source_interpretation.text: The reported cobalt-60 activity is 2.59×10^15 Bq and dose is 3.0×10^4 Gy. Activity does not specify dose rate or irradiation duration. The several-hour precipitation interval occurs after irradiation; the numerical 4 h applies only to vacuum drying.

source_interpretation.title: One typical specimen joins XRD and TEM
source_interpretation.text: The typical XRD sample is prepared from 0.05 kmol/m³ lead acetate in selenium-saturated ethylenediamine. The TEM text and caption explicitly identify the same sample. Cubic phase and 6.12 Å cell constant are XRD results; the 30 nm average is a TEM particle size, not a crystallite-size fit.

source_interpretation.title: Ambient synthesis does not replace the explicit drying condition
source_interpretation.text: The introduction describes room-temperature, ambient-pressure processing. The detailed workup explicitly ends in 4 h of vacuum drying at room temperature. Retain that specific vacuum condition rather than extending the generic pressure description into drying.

missingness: Both supplied main pages (875–876), both figures, full preparation/continuation, solvent controls, proposed interpretation and twelve references visually read. SI and cited full papers unreviewed. The scanned source has no verified text cache.

Lead acetate hydration, absolute precursor masses, solvent volume, numerical selenium saturation concentration, mixing/dissolution duration and addition order are unreported. The typical XRD/TEM sample is specifically tied to 0.05 kmol/m³ lead acetate in selenium-saturated ethylenediamine.

The 60Co source activity is 2.59×10^15 Bq and irradiation dose is 3.0×10^4 Gy. Irradiation duration, dose rate, source distance, energy spectrum, vessel and oxygen/purge conditions are unreported; no exposure time is derived.

Room temperature and ambient pressure are qualitative. The general ambient-pressure wording does not override the explicitly reported vacuum drying step. Several hours of post-irradiation standing is qualitative; only the vacuum drying time is numerically 4 h.

Collection technique, wash amounts/repetitions, dilute-acetic-acid concentration, vacuum level, drying apparatus, yield and storage are unreported. Wash order is absolute ethanol, distilled water, dilute acetic acid, then acetone.

Figure 2 explicitly depicts the same sample as Figure 1. No physical batch identifier, TEM specimen preparation/grid, XRD holder, particle-count statistic, size uncertainty or distribution width is given. Average TEM particle size is 30 nm; no XRD crystallite size is reported.

Benzene and tetrahydrofuran controls give neither a homogeneous selenium-containing solution nor PbSe under irradiation. Their charges, irradiation dose/time and subsequent processing are not individually stated and are not copied from the successful ethylenediamine route.

Formation chemistry is explicitly unknown and the solvent/solvated-electron explanation is proposed. No intermediate, kinetic rate, product atomic coordinates or current optical/electronic property measurement is supplied.
Generic molecular references and source-bound apparatus concepts are not measured solution, particle or apparatus geometry. Full molecular/crystal/presentation refinements remain pending.
